About.title: About Hermes
About.intro: How we bring trusted language models together in one chat.
About.overview: Hermes is an interface for chatting with LLMs. We don’t train our own model or present other models as ours. Hermes provides one interface, stores conversation history, and chooses a fallback model when the primary provider is temporarily unavailable.
About.short1: One interface for everyday chat, code, text analysis, photos, and video.
About.short2: Only specific models available in OpenRouter that passed a real API test.
About.short3: The server-side API key is never sent to the browser or shown to the user.
About.short4: Streaming responses, retries, and fallback routing during temporary provider failures.
About.what1: Hermes brings models with different capabilities into one chat. Some are better for photos and video, while others specialize in code, long context, or complex reasoning. The model is fixed to each conversation so its behavior doesn’t change unexpectedly.
About.what2: Hermes also prepares context, sends the necessary attachments, streams the response as it is generated, and stores history so you can return to the conversation.
About.request1: The browser sends text, part of the history, and any required attachments to the Hermes server.
About.request2: The server validates the model and request format, then calls OpenRouter with its own API key.
About.request3: OpenRouter selects available hosting for the chosen model and forwards the request.
About.request4: The response streams back; if a temporary failure occurs before it begins, Hermes can retry or switch models.
About.data1: Guest history is stored in the browser. Signed-in users can sync text history across devices. Files and video frames are sent to a model only when needed for the current request.
About.data2Before: OpenRouter does not log prompt and response text by default, but each downstream provider has its own rules. Do not send passwords, keys, or other secrets in chat. Learn more in the
About.autoText: Auto is local Hermes routing logic, not a separate model or a dynamic OpenRouter catalog. Text and multimodal requests use different short fallback lists. A model without photo or video support is never used for that kind of request.
About.modelsText: The catalog contains only specific versions. We verify OpenRouter availability, zero pricing, supported input formats, and a normal text response through the same API used by the chat.
About.limitsText: As of August 16, 2026, all listed versions have zero-priced input and output tokens in OpenRouter. Free pricing does not mean unlimited capacity: OpenRouter and providers can change daily limits, queues, and availability without notice. Hermes therefore cannot promise unlimited requests.
About.licensesText: Hermes receives responses through an API and does not distribute model weights. The weights remain with providers and are used remotely. Anyone distributing the weights or modified versions must preserve the notices, license copies, and attribution required by Apache 2.0, OpenMDW, and NVIDIA licenses. Direct license links are listed with each model above.
About.limitationsText: Model responses may be inaccurate, incomplete, or outdated. Hermes does not replace professional medical, legal, or financial review. High-stakes answers should be checked against reliable primary sources.

Help.title: Help
Help.intro: Everything you need to work confidently with chats, models, files, and your data.
Help.noticeText: Double-check important facts, calculations, and links. A model response is a useful starting point, not a final decision.
Help.startIntro: Your first request only takes three simple steps.
Help.step1Text: Each new chat starts a separate topic. This helps the model keep the right context and makes the conversation easier to find later.
Help.step2Text: Keep Auto if you are unsure, or choose a model for code, analysis, fast answers, photos, or video. The model is fixed to the chat after your first message.
Help.step3Text: Include context, constraints, and your preferred output format. Enter sends the message; Shift + Enter adds a new line.
Help.promptIntro: The clearer your request, the less the model has to guess.
Help.prompt1: State the goal first: describe exactly what the result should be.
Help.prompt2: Include the necessary context, source material, and examples.
Help.prompt3: Set constraints such as language, length, tone, deadline, or format.
Help.prompt4: Ask for missing details to be clarified and refine the result in the same chat.
Help.exampleText: Create a seven-slide presentation outline for beginner designers about typography basics. Give each slide a title and three short points. Use plain English and avoid professional jargon.
Help.featuresIntro: You can combine these tools within a single task.
Help.textFeatureText: Explain topics, edit writing, explore ideas, and work through code. Responses support lists, tables, formulas, and code blocks.
Help.mediaFeatureText: Attach up to four images or videos totaling no more than 3 MB. Hermes prepares key frames from video. A media-capable model is required.
Help.webFeatureText: Turn on Web for requests that depend on fresh information. You should still check dates, sources, and original documents.
Help.imageFeatureText: Describe a scene, choose a format and style, then save the best result in the separate image studio.
Help.dataIntro: Storage works differently depending on whether you are signed in.
Help.guestText: Chats are stored in the browser on this device only. Guests have a limit of five requests per week.
Help.accountText: Text history is available across your devices. Chat titles, favorites, and deletions are synchronized too.
Help.filesText: Photos, videos, and generated images are not synchronized to other devices. They are sent for processing only with the relevant request.
Help.troubleshootingIntro: Quick answers for the most common situations.
Help.attachmentQuestion: Why can’t I attach a file?
Help.attachmentAnswer: Hermes supports PNG, JPEG, WebP, and GIF images, plus MP4, MPEG, MOV, and WebM video. You can add up to four files totaling no more than 3 MB. If the chat is fixed to a model without media support, start a new chat and select Auto or a multimodal model.
Help.modelQuestion: Why did a different model answer?
Help.modelAnswer: If the selected model is temporarily unavailable before its response starts, Hermes may retry with a compatible fallback. The model that actually answered is shown next to the response.
Help.slowQuestion: Why is the response taking so long?
Help.slowAnswer: Free models can be queued or temporarily overloaded. Wait for the response to begin, stop it if needed, or try again later with another model.
Help.interruptedQuestion: What should I do if a response stops early?
Help.interruptedAnswer: The part already received is preserved. Retry the request or ask the model to continue where it stopped. If the problem persists, start a new chat or choose another model.
Help.storageQuestion: What if my browser runs out of storage?
Help.storageAnswer: Open Settings → Data. You can delete individual attachments, all local files, generated images, or chat history. Removing attachments does not erase the conversation text.
Help.safetyIntro: Do not share anything you would not send to an unfamiliar external service.
Help.safety1: Never send passwords, API keys, banking details, or other secrets.
Help.safety2: Have a qualified professional check medical, legal, and financial decisions.
Help.safety3: For important facts, request sources, open them, and verify the date, author, and content.
Help.stillText: Open a new chat and describe the task, expected result, and what you have already tried.

Hcode.title: Hermes Code
Hcode.intro: A practical guide to installing and using hcode — a local AI agent that understands the current project, can edit its files, and run development commands from your terminal.
Hcode.noticeTitle: hcode works inside the folder where you start it.
Hcode.noticeText: Open the project directory first, then run hcode. That directory becomes the fixed project boundary for the entire session.
Hcode.installIntro: The public release contains standalone binaries. Bun, Node.js, and a local build are not required for normal use.
Hcode.installStep1Text: You need macOS or Linux, curl, internet access, a terminal, and an OpenRouter API key. Windows binaries are not currently published.
Hcode.installStep2Text: Paste the command below into your terminal. It detects the operating system and processor architecture, then downloads the matching latest release from GitHub.
Hcode.installStep3Text: Open a new terminal and print the installed version. If the shell cannot find hcode yet, reload its configuration as described below.
Hcode.installerText: It writes the executable to ~/.local/bin/hcode, makes it executable, and adds ~/.local/bin to PATH in ~/.zshrc or ~/.bashrc when needed. It does not install a package manager or system service.
Hcode.firstRunIntro: Start hcode from the root of the project you want it to work on.
Hcode.firstStep1Text: On the first launch, the prompt hides your input and saves the key to ~/.hcode/config.json. If OPENROUTER_API_KEY is already set, that environment value is used instead.
Hcode.firstStep2Text: Ask in normal language. Include the desired result, relevant constraints, and the verification you expect. hcode responds in the same language as your request.
Hcode.firstStep3Text: Type y or yes only after checking the exact file or command shown in the prompt. Any other answer declines the action.
Hcode.promptExample: Find why the profile form does not save, make the smallest safe fix, and run the relevant tests. Preserve unrelated changes.
Hcode.workflowIntro: hcode combines an OpenRouter model with a small set of local project tools. The model plans the work; the executable performs only the requested local actions.
Hcode.flow1Text: The directory where hcode was launched is recorded as the project root. File tools cannot move outside it.
Hcode.flow2Text: Your message and conversation context are sent to OpenRouter. By default, hcode uses the openrouter/free route.
Hcode.flow3Text: The model may inspect the file tree, read text files, write files, or propose a shell command. Tool results are returned to the model for the next step.
Hcode.flow4Text: The agent can continue for up to 15 tool-call rounds, run proportionate checks, and then summarize what changed and what was verified.
Hcode.toolsIntro: Its toolset is deliberately compact and focused on everyday repository work.
Hcode.inspectText: Lists files recursively while ignoring dependencies, build output, Git internals, and secret environment files.
Hcode.readText: Reads UTF-8 text files with project-relative paths so the agent can understand existing code before changing it.
Hcode.writeText: Creates new text files or completely rewrites existing ones. Paths using parent traversal or escaping symlinks are rejected.
Hcode.runText: Runs a shell command from the project root, captures its exit code and output, and blocks known destructive or privileged commands.
Hcode.permissionsText: listing and reading happen without a prompt; creating a new file can also happen directly. Rewriting an existing file and every shell command require your confirmation. Always review the proposed action before answering yes.
Hcode.commandsIntro: Slash commands work inside an interactive session. Flags are run directly from your shell.
Hcode.commandClear: Clear the screen and the current conversation history. Project files are not affected.
Hcode.commandVersion: Print the current hcode version inside the session.
Hcode.commandUpdate: Ask for confirmation, install the latest GitHub release, and tell you to restart hcode.
Hcode.commandChange: Replace the OpenRouter API key and use the new key immediately in the current session.
Hcode.commandResetKey: Delete the saved API key. Restart hcode to configure it again.
Hcode.commandVersionFlag: Print the version without starting an interactive chat.
Hcode.commandUpdateFlag: Open the update confirmation without starting a chat.
Hcode.configurationIntro: Environment variables let you override credentials, the model route, and terminal rendering without changing the saved config.
Hcode.envKey: Uses this OpenRouter key before checking the saved config. Useful for CI or temporary sessions.
Hcode.envModel: Selects a specific OpenRouter model instead of openrouter/free. Use a valid provider/model-name identifier.
Hcode.envImage: Overrides logo rendering. Accepted values are iterm, kitty, or text; otherwise hcode detects common terminals automatically.
Hcode.envColor: Set this variable to disable ANSI colors in terminal output.
Hcode.securityIntro: hcode is local software, but model requests are processed remotely through OpenRouter. Treat repository access and credentials accordingly.
Hcode.security1: The saved key is stored in ~/.hcode/config.json with user-only file permissions (0600); the ~/.hcode directory is created with mode 0700.
Hcode.security2: The project boundary is validated for file operations, parent path segments are refused, and listed symbolic links are skipped.
Hcode.security3: The file list excludes .env and .env.* secrets, except documented example, sample, and template files. Do not paste secrets into prompts or source files.
Hcode.security4: Review generated code, diffs, and command output. An AI agent can misunderstand a task or produce incorrect code even when a command succeeds.
Hcode.updatesText: The updater reruns the official installer and replaces the binary with the asset from GitHub’s latest release. You can update inside hcode with /update or from the shell:
Hcode.releaseCheckedBefore: The current public release is hcode 0.1.2. Repository and release information checked on
Hcode.troubleshootingIntro: Most startup issues can be resolved with the checks below.
Hcode.notFoundText: Restart the terminal or run source ~/.zshrc for Zsh and source ~/.bashrc for Bash. Then check that ~/.local/bin is present in PATH.
Hcode.keyText: Use /change to enter another key for the current session, or /reset-key and restart. Also verify that the key is active in your OpenRouter account.
Hcode.networkText: Check your connection and whether GitHub and openrouter.ai are reachable. An HTTP error from OpenRouter is displayed in the terminal with its status and message.
Hcode.unsupportedText: The installer currently accepts Darwin or Linux on arm64/aarch64 and x86_64/amd64. Use one of the published platforms or build the project from source with Bun.
Hcode.uninstallText: Remove the installed executable with the command below. This leaves your shell PATH entry and saved API key untouched.
Hcode.configRemovalText: To remove the saved credential as well, run /reset-key before uninstalling, or delete ~/.hcode/config.json yourself.
Hcode.footerTitle: Read the source, report an issue, or follow releases
Hcode.footerText: hcode is developed openly in tetttet/hcode. GitHub contains the installer, TypeScript source, and binaries for every published platform.
